summary.headline: Lumax Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% y-o-y to INR 1,342 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% on raw-material pass-through lag; FY27 double-digit margin guidance retained.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR 1,342 crore (+33% y-o-y, +10% q-o-q), with H1 revenue at INR 2,565 crore (+33% y-o-y). Consolidated EBITDA was INR 110 crore (+21% y-o-y) with margin of 8.2% versus 9.0% a year earlier, as West Asia-driven material and electronic component cost increases were only partly recovered from customers. PAT including associates was INR 52 crore (+46% y-o-y), margin 3.9%. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 25%+ from 20%+ and kept the full-year double-digit EBITDA margin target, which depends on H2 recovery of escalations.

financial_highlights.change: +21% y-o-y; margin vs 9% in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: PAT incl. share of associates (Q2 FY27)
Material cost impact on H1 margin

segments.name: LED lighting
segments.commentary: LED was 63% of H1 FY27 revenue vs 61% in H1 FY26; about 80% of the order book (management also cited ~88% on another slide in the call). LED penetration at the company is ~65%, versus ~30% five to seven years ago.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Passenger vehicles are 63% of the order book. Key launches were Tata Aeris tail lamps and M&M Thar Refresh headlamp, fog, cornering and side repeater lamps.

segments.name: 2/3-wheelers
segments.commentary: 2/3-wheelers are 37% of the order book. New or expanded business with TVS, Suzuki 2W, Yamaha and Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI tail lamp wallet share targeted at ~50% from under 20%).

segments.name: EV
segments.commentary: EV contributed ~10-12% of business and ~11% of the order book; management says the product is powertrain-agnostic.

segments.name: Other OEMs
segments.commentary: Management said 'other' customers were ~12% of Q2 revenue and named JD (John Deere), Škoda Volkswagen, TVS and Ashok Leyland as main contributors.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 25%+ from 20%+; H2 growth will be lower than H1's ~35% because of a higher H2 FY26 base, but H2 q-o-q revenue is expected to keep rising.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided to double digits; H2 margin implied at ~10.5-11%, with Q3 lower than Q4, contingent on recovering Q1 and Q2 material escalations.
Caveat: management would need to relook at guidance if West Asia-related volatility continues.
FY27 capex guidance maintained at INR 200-250 crore; ~INR 80 crore spent in H1.
FY28: ~60% of the current order book (close to INR 1,500 crore revenue) is due for SOP; management is 'quite bullish' on FY28.
Management reported a ~20% wallet-share gain at 4-5 OEMs over two years, and export revenue is expected only in 2-3 years and will be minuscule.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance INR 200-250 crore; INR ~80 crore spent in H1, remainder in H2 projects.
Projects are progressing as planned; several launched programs are scheduled to reach SOP by end-FY27 or early FY28.

Localization: bare PCB ~60-70% localized; SMT is 100% in-house captive; connectors ~30-35%; LED modules only partly localized. Overall LED localization ~30-35% today, targeted above 50% over the next ~3 years.
Management is in talks with Stanley on localizing LED chips and light control modules, but has no firm plan yet.
demand_pricing: Industry: Q2 FY27 auto production 106 lakh units (+19% y-o-y); PV ~17 lakh (+25%), 2W ~81 lakh (+17%), 3W ~4.5 lakh (+25%), CV ~3.5 lakh (+34%). Management expects growth to ease in H2.
Raw-material escalations (polymers, electronic components, freight, rupee) passed through with a lag; recovery of Q1 escalation is incomplete and Q2 escalations are expected to hit P&L in Q3.
Management said price increases from raw-material escalations raise revenue but dilute EBITDA margin.

Wallet-share targets: Maruti Suzuki (largest order book share) 25-30% to 35-40% in 2-3 years; Suzuki 2W 15-20% to 30%+; Škoda/VW tail lamp ~30% to ~70%; Toyota Kirloskar front lighting 15-20% (new headlamp award); HMSI headlamp 60-70% unchanged.
Industry LED penetration: ~63-65% overall, PV ~55-60%, 2W/3W 75-80%; management says ADB adoption will take 3-5 years and is currently limited to a couple of models.
Competition: top 5 Indian lighting players expected to retain control; new OE entrants are mostly niche. Management said there is no wallet-share decline at any OEM.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in double-digit FY27 EBITDA margin given cost pressures and recovery lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 and Q2 escalations are being recovered in H2, no major further price hikes are expected, and operating leverage will help. H2 margin is expected at ~10.5-11%, lower in Q3 and higher in Q4; guidance is conditional on no major West Asia volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth slow after the festive season, and what is the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 growth will be well below H1's ~35% due to the high base, but q-o-q revenue should keep rising. FY27 growth is now 25%+; about 60% of the order book (~INR 1,500 crore) is due for SOP in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is export a growth driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Export engagement with OEM international purchasing offices is ongoing, but it takes 2-3 years to convert; the domestic market remains the priority.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete with integrated ADAS/lighting players, and what technology roadmap exists?
qa_highlights.answer: ADB has no camera integration today. Management relies on Stanley for localized technology and on the Czech and Taiwan engineering centres for projection, OLED, DLP and laser technologies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LED and PCB localization status, and does the company have PLI benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Bare PCB ~60-70% localized, SMT in-house, connectors ~30-35%. Management clarified that auto lighting is not covered under the PLI scheme.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Hyundai investment, and what is the role of the associate?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyundai business is handled by associate SL Lumax, so no direct impact on Lumax Industries. The company is talking to Hyundai directly about possible supply to them as a de-risking step.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the revenue growth in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth across most segments, higher LED and ADB content per vehicle, raw-material price pass-through, and wallet-share gains at certain OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and FY28 outlook beyond the current capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR 200-250 crore, with INR ~80 crore spent in H1. Projects go live around end-FY27 or early FY28, and FY28 SOP revenue is expected at ~INR 1,500 crore plus.

risks_watch: Raw-material and electronic component escalations: Q2 cost increases hit P&L in Q3, and margin recovery depends on customer pass-through lag.
West Asia conflict and energy/shipping disruption could force management to revisit the FY27 double-digit margin guidance.

Supply-chain volatility in imported electronics (25-30% of materials imported, mainly LED chips and electronics) may cause customer production shortfalls, though management sees no production schedule pullback for H2.
Rupee depreciation adds to import costs; localization timelines (LED chips, light control modules) are still undecided.
H2 growth slowdown against a high base; Hero MotoCorp revenue share fell from 8% to 6%, attributed by management to product mix.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and margin targets, but cautious on near-term cost pressure, with the margin guidance explicitly conditional on no major further West Asia volatility. Evasive on specifics for localization plans, PLI status and exports, and on competitor localization.
key_quotes: And hence, the guidance, which Ravi had mentioned for the full year, is still intact to deliver a double-digit EBITDA margin.
So, for H2, we will not be definitely looking at a 35% growth.
The Company has its own Czech and Taiwan advanced engineering centres, and this is where all the advanced technologies are being developed.
Anything outside of the lighting domain, we will capture in the other group company.

adds.what: FY27 capex INR 200-250 crore for H2 projects; several launched programs reaching SOP by end-FY27 or early FY28 (capacity not quantified)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 25%+ from 20%+, backed by a INR 2,580 crore order book (~60% due for SOP in FY28, ~INR 1,500 crore revenue) and H1 revenue up 33%, though H2 growth is guided lower than H1's ~35% on a higher base and no new capacity is quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides H2 EBITDA margin at ~10.5-11% vs 8.2% in Q2, as Q1 and Q2 material escalations are recovered; the ~100-120 bps H1 material hit reverses only if pass-through completes and no major West Asia volatility recurs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 capex of INR 200-250 crore (about INR 80 crore spent in H1) funds H2 projects, with several launched programs reaching SOP by end-FY27 or early FY28; capacity is not quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue rose 33% y-o-y to INR 2,565 crore and the order book is INR 2,580 crore, with ~60% (about INR 1,500 crore) due for SOP in FY28, though H2 growth slows from H1's ~35% on a higher base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, so the need for new capex is unclear; the INR 1,500 crore SOP wave in FY28 and the Stanley LED-chip localization talks (no firm plan) could trigger one, but nothing is committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was already raised to 25%+ from 20%+, and H1 growth was ~33%; a further raise depends on H2 holding up, which is clouded by the West Asia risk.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 escalations hit the P&L in Q3, and management says it would need to relook at the double-digit margin guidance if West Asia volatility continues; Q2 margin was 8.2%, below 9.0% a year earlier.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Recent launches include Tata Aeris tail lamps and M&M Thar Refresh headlamp, and FY28 SOP of about INR 1,500 crore is tied to new programs; no specific new product dates were given.

rows.label: FY28 SOP wave of ~INR 1,500 crore
rows.why: About 60% of the INR 2,580 crore order book (close to INR 1,500 crore revenue) is due for SOP in FY28, and management is 'quite bullish' on FY28.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA down to 2.2x
rows.why: Net long-term debt fell to INR 188 crore at 30 Sep 2026 from INR 291 crore at 31 Mar 2025, and net debt/EBITDA is 2.2x versus 3.0x.

rows.label: Export revenue
rows.why: Management says export revenue is 2-3 years away and will be minuscule, with the domestic market the priority.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27 growth raise and the double-digit margin target, but cautious on raw-material pass-through and West Asia risk, and evasive on localization, PLI and export specifics; analysts probed margin recovery, the H2 slowdown and FY28 visibility.
